summary: Lore Sander worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, having studied under Ernst Waldschmidt (c. 1961–1967). She served as Curator at the Museum of Asian Art (1987) and lectured at the Free University of Berlin (1994).

Lori Meeks specializes in Buddhist, Japanese, and religious studies. Educated at Columbia University and Princeton University (PhD c. 1998–2003 under Jacqueline I. Stone), she held posts at Stanford University (c. 2003–2004) and the University of Southern California (c. 2004).

Lorna Dewaraja worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Ceylon and the University of London, she held posts at the University of Colombo and served as Associate Professor of History at the University of Peradeniya.

Lorne Ladner works in Buddhist studies and counseling. He studied under traditional teacher Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche and served as an adjunct faculty member at Argosy University, both attested in 2004.

Lothar Ledderose is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and art history. He studied at Heidelberg, Bonn, Princeton, Harvard, Tokyo, and Cologne, and served as a professor at Heidelberg University (c. 1976–2010) and president of DMG (1978–1990).

Sinologist and archaeologist Lothar von Falkenhausen studied at Bonn, Peking University, Kyoto, and Harvard (PhD c. 1982–1988). Following posts at Stanford and UC Riverside, he became a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1993.

Louis Dumont specialized in Indology and religious studies, studying under Marcel Mauss and Walther Schubring. He held posts at the Musée National des Arts et Traditions Populaires, the University of Oxford (1951–1955), and the EPHE/EHESS (1955).

Louis Finot worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. An alumnus of the École des Chartes, he served as director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient from 1898 and professeur honoraire at the Collège de France (1920–1930).
Louis Gabaude specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He held a post at the École française d'Extrême-Orient from circa 1980 to 2007.

Louis Gernet studied at the École Normale Supérieure (c. 1902–1905) and worked in history and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Algiers (c. 1917–1948) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (c. 1948–1962).

Linguist Louis Havet studied at EPHE under Michel Bréal, Gaston Paris, and Abel Bergaigne. He served as professor and Latin philology department chair at the Collège de France (1885–1925) and vice-president of Association Guillaume Budé (1917).

Linguist and Indologist Louis Herbert Gray studied at Princeton (c. 1892–1896) and Columbia University (PhD c. 1896–1900). He held posts at Princeton University (c. 1900–1902) and the University of Nebraska-Lincoln (1921).

Sinologist and religious studies scholar Louis Komjathy earned his PhD at Boston University under Paul Rouzer. In 2014, he was attested as Assistant Professor of Chinese Religions and Comparative Religious Studies at the University of San Diego.

Indologist and linguist Louis Renou studied at EPHE under Antoine Meillet and Jules Bloch. He held major posts at the University of Lyon, the University of Paris (c. 1937–1966), and served as Director at the Collège de France.

Louis de La Vallée Poussin studied at Liège, KU Leuven, Paris, and Leiden under Lévi, Kern, and others. Specializing in Indology and Buddhist studies, he held a professorship at Ghent University from 1893 to 1929.

Louis-Mathieu Langlès worked in Sinology, Indology, and Iranian studies, studying at the Collège de France under Silvestre de Sacy. He served at the Bibliothèque nationale de France and directed the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (1795–1824).

Louise Child works in religious studies and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Leeds under Linda Hogan, studied under traditional teacher Ringu Tulku, and taught at the University of Leeds.

Loukram Ibempishak Devi works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Gauhati University under Sibnath Sarma and also studied under S. Shyamkishor Singh and S. Lokendrajit Singh (attested 1999).
Lozang Samten studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche.
Lozang Tenpa studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche.
